questions.stem: A 7-year-old is diagnosed with a genetic mutation leading to impaired cleavage of the FGF-23 protein. Which of the following clinical findings would be expected:
questions.note:
**FGF-23 that can't be cleaved builds up, and the answer slide says it blocks calcitriol synthesis, leading to vitamin D deficiency and rickets in a child.** Slide 51 marks B in red. This lecture has slides only, no recording.

Hyperphosphatemia: false. Slide 46 lists hypophosphatemia with hyperphosphaturia as the result of high FGF-23, so phosphate goes down, not up.

Impaired bone mineralization: true. Less calcitriol plus phosphate wasting means bone can't mineralize properly, which is rickets in a child. Slide 46 names autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets among the genetic causes.

Hypercalcemia: false. Calcitriol drives intestinal and renal calcium absorption (slide 41), so losing it does not raise calcium.

Hypermagnesemia: false. Magnesium doesn't appear anywhere in the FGF-23 slides (41, 46).
